$comment: Canonical Story Block fixtures for #37340. ONE source of truth, shared by all five renderer implementations (VTL, React, Vue, Angular standard, Angular semantic) so they cannot silently diverge — see specs/37340-emoji-text-node/contracts/renderer.contract.md C4. These payloads are only ever RENDERED, never re-saved: that is what proves AC-019.

shape1_emojiSplitsLink.$comment: The reported customer payload. Emoji typed INTO already-linked text: the node carries NO marks and sits BETWEEN the two linked text nodes, so plain adjacency merging cannot fix it. Expect ONE <a> containing ©.

shape2_emojiCarriesLink.$comment: Link applied OVER an existing emoji node. Already renders as one <a> today; must not regress.

differingLinkAttrs.$comment: Link marks differ by href — the run MUST break. Guards against over-eager coalescing.

nonEmojiAtomBreaksRun.$comment: AC-016. An intervening unmarked atom that is NOT an emoji must NOT be absorbed. Absorption is deliberately narrow.

boldNestedInLink.$comment: AC-018. Other marks still nest correctly INSIDE the single coalesced <a>.

unresolvableName.$comment: AC-013 + security. `name` arrives from the Contentlet REST API with no schema validation, so it is user-controlled. The :name: fallback MUST be HTML-escaped and MUST warn once.

unresolvableNameWithHtml.$comment: XSS guard — must render escaped, never as live markup.

emojiNodeWithTextAttr.$comment: Fallback precedence step 2: an unresolvable name but the node carries `text`, so that wins over :name:.

mixedRepresentation.$comment: Contract C4. After the fix one field may hold a legacy emoji NODE and a literal CHARACTER side by side. Both halves must render identically — this is what makes mixed representation safe.

noOp.$comment: Nothing to coalesce. Output must be byte-identical to today — this guards the every-page render path.
